ready.title: Ready
ready.description: Verify and open the right view

welcome.title: Welcome to ORGII
welcome.description: Let's configure your workspace in a few quick steps.

devPassport.title: Set up Dev Passport
devPassport.description: Every vibe engineer needs an identity.

github.title: Connect GitHub
github.description: Connect your GitHub account to access repos, create commits, and manage pull requests directly from ORGII.
github.hint: You can also connect GitHub later from Settings > Integrations

workspace.title: Open a Workspace
workspace.description: Open a local folder or clone a repo to start working. ORGII will automatically index your codebase for intelligent code assistance.
workspace.hint: You can skip this step and open a workspace later

theme.title: Choose Your Theme
theme.description: Select a theme that suits your preference. You can change this anytime in Settings.

complete.title: You're All Set!
complete.description: Your workspace is ready. Start a new session to begin coding with AI assistance, or explore the app to discover all features.

hero.title: Let's set up your <brand>ORGII</brand>
hero.description: A few quick choices to personalize your workspace.

classicPanel.title: Make ORGII feel like yours
classicPanel.description: Choose a comfortable language, appearance, theme, and accent color. You can change them anytime.

sidebar.subtitle: Choose your language and appearance. Everything else stays available in the app.
sidebar.help: Completed steps stay editable. Future steps unlock as you finish.

goal.title: What do you want to accomplish first?
goal.description: ORGII will adapt setup and take you to the right product surface when you finish.
goal.hint: This changes the setup path; it does not permanently limit what you can use.

personal.title: Start an agent session
personal.description: Set up a personal coding workflow and open the Launchpad.

team.title: See team Codex activity
team.description: Connect an organization, choose repo visibility, and open Team Inbox.

work.title: Manage work
work.description: Understand Projects and Work Items, then create the first item.

tools.title: Detect your coding tools
tools.description: Check Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor using the existing local validation service.
tools.privacy: Secrets never enter setup state. Only provider, count, and validation status are retained.

organization.title: Connect the team organization
organization.description: Sign in once, then select an existing organization, create one, or join with an invite.
organization.signInHint: Team activity uses an ORG2 Cloud account so members share the same organization boundary.
organization.invitePlaceholder: Paste the link your admin shared

sharing.title: Choose what the team can see
sharing.description: The repository remote is the visibility boundary. Sharing level controls how much session detail is published.
sharing.workspaceDescription: The local folder where your agent runs
sharing.repoScopeDescription: Resolve normalized Git remotes from the current workspace
sharing.levelDescription: Applied by the organization to matching sessions
sharing.verified: The server accepted this repository policy and the sync queue drained.
sharing.memberHint: {{org}} is managed by an admin. Your local Codex history is ready to sync under their repository policy.
sharing.memberVerified: Your organization selection is active and the current sync request drained.

basics.title: Basic preferences
basics.description: You can always change these later.
basics.workspaceDescription: Sessions run against files in a workspace; projects and work items organize work rather than replace the filesystem.
basics.settingsHint: Tools, workspaces, organizations, team visibility, and tutorials can be configured later from the app.

tutorial.title: Pick one contextual tutorial
tutorial.description: It starts after setup, on the real product surface where the controls exist.
tutorial.hint: You can replay either tutorial later from the Settings menu.

model.title: How ORGII work fits together
model.description: These objects solve different problems; none of them is another name for a folder.

session.title: Session
session.description: A conversation and execution context for an agent. It may reference one workspace.

workItem.title: Work Item
workItem.description: A trackable task with status, assignee, discussion, and linked sessions.

project.title: Project
project.description: A planning container for Work Items. It may coordinate work across repositories.

workspace.title: Workspace / filesystem
workspace.description: The real local folders and files agents read and modify.

model.relationship: Project → Work Item → Session → Workspace files

ready.title: Setup is ready
ready.description: Review the durable checks below, then open the surface that matches your original goal.
ready.toolsLater: Agent access can be added later
ready.destinationHint: Your setup progress remains persisted after restart.
ready.teamDestinationHint: Your selected organization and setup progress remain persisted after restart.

errors.signInRequired: Sign in to ORG2 Cloud first.
errors.sessionExpired: Your ORG2 Cloud session expired. Sign in again.
errors.invalidInvite: This invite link or code is invalid.
errors.rosterNotConverged: The organization is not visible in your refreshed membership list yet.
errors.cloudUnavailable: ORG2 Cloud is unavailable. Try again.
errors.unknown: The setup operation failed. Try again.
errors.workspaceRequired: Open a workspace before configuring team scope.
errors.gitRemoteRequired: This workspace has no Git remote. Add a remote, then try again.
errors.orgAndScopeRequired: Select an organization and repository scope first.
errors.policyChanged: Team settings changed while saving. Review and verify them again.
errors.inviteOrgChanged: The selected organization changed while creating the invite. Try again.
errors.syncOrgChanged: The selected organization changed while verifying sync. Try again.

generalLayout.title: General layout tour
generalLayout.description: Learn the Session sidebar, Chat Panel, station mode switcher, Workstation, dock, and app areas.

chat-panel.title: Chat Panel
chat-panel.body: This is where users have conversations with agents, review activity, and send follow-up instructions.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.body: View your own usage and runtime status here. In an organization, you can also inspect member sync status and open a member to review Codex, Claude, and Cursor usage.

station-mode-pill.title: Switch station modes
station-mode-pill.body: Use this pill to switch station modes. Desktop means My Station, your workspace. Infinity means Agent Station, the agent activity view.

dock.title: Agent Station dock
dock.body: The dock switches apps inside the station. The tour temporarily disables auto-hide so these controls stay visible.

all-tabs.title: All Tabs
all-tabs.body: The first dock icon shows all open tabs together, regardless of which workstation app owns them.

code-editor.title: Code Editor
code-editor.body: Use Code Editor for files, diffs, terminals, source control, and coding changes made during a session.

browser.title: Browser
browser.body: Use Browser for web pages, previews, app testing, and browser-based investigation alongside the chat.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: Use Projects to track work items, plans, and project state connected to the current workspace.

codeEditor.title: Code Editor tour
codeEditor.description: Learn tabs, repo and branch switching, Source Control, Git History, and the project dashboard.

tabs.title: Code Editor tabs
tabs.body: Tabs collect the files, diffs, terminals, source control views, and dashboards you open while working in the repo.

repo-selector.title: Create or switch repos
repo-selector.body: Use the repo selector to switch the active repo or add another repository or workspace.

branch-selector.title: Change branches
branch-selector.body: The branch selector shows the current Git branch and opens the branch switch or create flow for this repo.

editor-surface.title: Editor workspace
editor-surface.body: This is the main Code Editor surface. Open files, inspect diffs, run terminals, and review generated changes here.

create-tabs.title: Create new tabs
create-tabs.body: Use the plus menu in All Tabs to create terminals, browser tabs, files, dashboards, and repo utilities.

source-control.title: Git changes
source-control.body: Open Source Control to review changed files, stage or unstage work, commit, pull, push, fetch, and sync with the remote.

git-history.title: Git history
git-history.body: Git History switches Source Control into commit history mode so you can inspect previous commits and related changes.

dashboard.title: Code Editor dashboard
dashboard.body: The dashboard is the Code Editor home tab for workspaces. Use it to add repos, open repo details, and jump into project work.
